contract: firmware/ALIVE.md section 3 (1.0.0-cc5.4 frame fields; PRESENTATION_V4.md otherwise)
about: Shared parser-parity fixtures for the ALIVE.md section 3 frame fields (clock, playing, progress, feedback.skip, ledDrive, ledDither), same case format as frames_v4.json plus `alive`. Each case: name, note, capabilities, input, expect {accept, output} describing the HOST adapter (control_center/device.py _frame) for those capabilities, rawParity, and alive {accept, stored?}: what a 1.0.0-cc5.4 parser (src/cc_frame_parse.cpp) does with `input` itself.

rules.host: device._frame(input, capabilities) returns exactly expect.output (key order included): it never raises for a section 3 field.
rules.firmwareOutput: A 1.0.0-cc5.4 parser accepts every expect.output and stores its text byte-identically and its section 3 fields as sent (playing only on Home layouts, skip only with kind ok).
rules.firmwareRaw: As in frames_v4.json: when rawParity is true, the parser fed input directly accepts it and stores the same text as expect.output.
rules.aliveRaw: Every case: the parser fed input directly accepts it exactly when alive.accept, and then stores alive.stored (playing -1|0|1, feedbackSkip -1|0|1, clock/progress/ledDrive/ledDither or null when absent). device.alive_parse(input) returns the same (stored, no invalid field) or names the invalid field(s). Both parsers validate first, on every layout and feedback kind (invalid -> reject), then strip a valid playing outside nowPlaying/volume/idle/notice and a valid skip with a kind other than ok.
rules.gating: Without capabilities.alive.version == 1 (an int) on presentation >= 4 the host output is exactly desktop v6's for the same input (gate-* cases were produced by the unmodified v6 device.py).
rules.budget: With alive the section 8 budget reserves the longest clock, progress, ledDrive and ledDither, so a frame line with all of them added at send time is <= 1,100 B.
